title: Next Iteration Planning
description: From recent pages and experiments, assesses what is done versus blocked and proposes next-iteration goals and priorities, framing risk as risk-to-progress.

steps.prompt: Summarize what has been accomplished versus what remains blocked or incomplete based on the iteration pages and recent experiments. For each item, note whether it is: done, in-progress, blocked, or not-yet-started. Use this rubric to rate the risk-to-progress — 1: on track, no blockers; 2: minor delays, workarounds available; 3: one significant blocker requiring action this week; 4: multiple blockers, milestone at risk; 5: critical block, iteration cannot proceed without resolution. Cite specific page notes or experiment outcomes from the context. List 3-5 actions to unblock the highest-priority items.

Identify technical risks or knowledge gaps that could derail the next iteration. Consider: experiments with anomalous or unexplained results, parameters that have not converged, equipment limitations encountered, missing baseline data, and unresolved scientific questions from prior iterations. Use this rubric — 1: no unresolved technical issues; 2: minor unknowns, answerable in current iteration; 3: one unexplained result that could change direction; 4: fundamental technical uncertainty, next steps unclear; 5: prior results invalidate the current approach. Cite specific experiment IDs or page references. Provide 3-5 mitigations.

Assess whether the proposed or implied next steps are sequenced correctly and are resource-feasible. Consider: whether experiments depend on samples or data not yet available, instrument availability, whether parallel work is possible, and whether the iteration scope is realistic. Use this rubric — 1: well-sequenced, all dependencies satisfied; 2: minor dependency risk, manageable; 3: one key dependency not yet satisfied; 4: multiple unresolved dependencies, scope must be cut; 5: next iteration cannot start without external inputs not in progress. Cite specific dependencies visible in the context. List 3-5 concrete sequencing or resourcing mitigations.
